publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Accurate stock price prediction is a challenging yet crucial goal in finance, with significant implications for investment decisions and risk management. This paper presents a comprehensive review of machine learning techniques for stock price prediction, examining traditional methods such as regression and ensemble models, as well as advanced approaches that integrate sentiment analysis and textual data sources. With the emergence of powerful Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Llama and Gemini, we explore their potential for enhancing predictive accuracy using historical stock data. Key challenges are discussed, including data quality, model interpretability, and adapting to dynamic market conditions. Additionally, this paper proposes a trustworthy stock price prediction model based on LLMs enabling informed investment decision-making. Experimental results demonstrate that ChatGPT-4o model achieved a prediction accuracy of approximately 97%, which can be improved by tuning model parameters. Consequently, the paper highlights the potential of LLMs in improving stock price forecasting.

articleTitle: Scalable Smart Home Management with ESP32-S3: A Low-Cost Solution for Accessible Home Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Assistive technology plays a crucial role in enhancing the quality of life, independence and emotional well-being of individuals with disabilities. Despite advancements in this field, there remains limited use of internet-based remote controllers in assistive devices. This paper presents a cost-effective., internet-connected universal remote-control system based on the ESP32-S3 System on Chip (SoC) capable of controlling multiple home devices such as TVs, air conditioners, smart appliances, and lighting via smartphones or tablets. The proposed system integrates competitive features like cost-effectiveness, low power, high-performance wireless communication (Wi-Fi and Bluetooth) in addition to a high level of scalability. By leveraging the capabilities of the ESP32-S3 chip, we offer an efficient solution for home automation, a promising area within assistive technology. The paper also highlights the importance of intuitive and accessible control interfaces to increase user autonomy among people with physical disabilities.

articleTitle: AR-Base Educational Mobile Application for Pet Care Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: This research proposes an innovative mobile application designed to enhance pet care management by assisting dog owners in understanding and addressing various aspects of dog care. The application incorporates three key components: Augmented Reality (AR) guidance for capturing dog skin conditions, Image Processing to determine dog skin conditions, breed, life stage, and body condition, and video analysis to assess dog behaviors. By integrating advanced machine learning models, including DenseNet121, Xception, and YOLO v5 algorithm, along with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), the application aims to provide accurate health assessments and recommendations. The goal of this research is to enhance pet care practices through the use of innovative technology, enabling users to make informed decisions regarding their dogs' health, nutrition, behaviors, and overall well-being.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Personalized Fitness Coaching with Body Type-Based Workout and Nutrition Plans and Real-Time Exercise Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: In today's fast-paced world filled with distractions such as work, family, education and other commitments, people often have little time and energy to maintain a healthy lifestyle. Traditional fitness approaches frequently fail to meet the dynamic needs and expectations of modern users, leading to dissatisfaction and disengagement. A main problem of traditional systems is the lack of personalization for diverse users, that also monitors and tracks the workout progression. This study introduces an innovative system that creates a personalized workout and diet plan which aims to engage and motivate the user experience by individual personalization. Through means such as real-time exercise tracking and feedback mechanisms, this mobile fitness application aims to address limitations of traditional fitness approaches, proving fitness experience for users to achieve their health and fitness goals in a convenient and sustainable manner

articleTitle: Fog-Enabled Metaverse: Common Points in an Industry 5.0 Context
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: The industrial Metaverse is a virtual world where people and smart machines can meet, work, and interact. It is a constantly evolving domain where physical production assets such as machines, factories, grids, and transportation systems, along with human operators, are represented by interactive virtual objects. However, creating such a virtual world requires an efficient process for data collection, processing, and transmission that can meet real-time requirements. To address this challenge, Fog-based architecture has been designed to cope with the massive data processing and transmission needs by splitting the processing task over a set of parallel Fog nodes. This technology is more cost-effective and efficient for industries. In this paper, we explore the use of the Fog computing architecture for deploying industrial metaverse applications. We identify and explain the challenges that arise during this deployment, with the aim of facilitating their resolution. To meet the real-time requirements of Industry 5.0 application, we propose an industrial metaverse architecture based on Fog-computing nodes. This architecture will enable efficient data collection, processing, and transmission while providing a virtual world where people and machines can interact seamlessly.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach for Brain Tumor Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: The medical field is incredibly stressful for both specialists and patients, especially when dealing with life threatening cases. Brain tumor identification is one of the most challenging tasks even for experts in the field. Fortunately, the evolution of machine learning techniques and their flexibility to be integrated into many different fields, including tumor identification and classification has greatly simplified this task. For the physicians to accurately diagnose a patient, they must first have a lot of knowledge and years of experience in addition to going through many cases. Machine learning simplifies this process when it comes to learning and using this knowledge to decide without human intervention. If the data fed to the model is accurate, the decisions made will be more accurate. In this paper, an automated machine learning model is developed to identify brain tumors. Different datasets are utilized in the developed model. The accuracy achieved by the model lies between 60% and 70%. Another dataset is then used, and the model shows an accuracy of 99%, precision of 83%, F1 score of 77% and recall of 75%.

articleTitle: Enhancing Medical Image Classification with Streamlined-EvidNet: A Robust Neural Network Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Accurate classification of medical images is crucial for automated analysis and disease diagnosis. Traditional deep learning methods often struggle with challenges such as variations in image quality and imbalanced datasets, leading to diagnostic errors. This study introduces an advanced framework that integrates contrastive learning, ResNet architectures, and Bayesian methods to enhance the accuracy and reliability of medical image classification, with a focus on heart disease detection. Contrastive learning enhances the model's capability to differentiate between similar and dissimilar image pairs, thereby reducing the challenges posed by imbalanced datasets. ResNet architectures provide robust feature extraction, while Bayesian methods offer probabilistic interpretations, addressing uncertainty in predictions. Our comprehensive evaluation demonstrates significant improvements in classification performance, positioning this approach as a promising tool for clinical applications in radiology. The proposed framework effectively overcomes challenges associated with variable image quality and imbalanced datasets, contributing to improved diagnostic accuracy and reliability in cardiovascular disease detection.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach for Detecting Diabetic Retinopathy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: The World Health Organization (WHO) reports that diabetic retinopathy affects one-third of diabetics, regardless of their stage of the disease. Several research efforts are focused on its automated detection and diagnosis. Identifying diabetic retinopathy is crucial due to the damage that occurs to the blood vessels of the eye retina, leading to vision blur or even complete blindness. Thus, an annual checkup is needed for people with diabetes. Moreover, uncontrolled sugar levels for diabetes patients could worsen the current stage of diabetic retinopathy. Consequently, automated detection can greatly contribute to the treatment of disease. This can be carried out through several algorithms, including deep learning models and support vector machines, in addition to transfer learning. This contribution proposes a new approach for diabetic retinopathy automated detection based on convolutional neural network (CNN) models. The proposed model provides both binary and multi-class detection. Both scenarios have shown promising results, where the training accuracies of both the binary classification and the multi-class are 92% and 94%, respectively.

articleTitle: Flexible Granular Deep Learning Voting Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: The recognition of sleep stages is a very complex and novel topic for many physicians. In an attempt to capitalise on the advances in this field of computing, a number of machine learning algorithms have attempted to replicate the actions that physicians conduct. Deep learning researchers are attempting to create and assess a variety of models and building blocks to assist physicians with their analysis because the polysomnograph's structure is a challenging combination of reasonably comparable components. In this work, we present a broad yet adaptable architecture that leverages the main driving force behind voting systems to enable scientists and doctors to incorporate as many criteria or blocks as required.

articleTitle: Enhancing Highway Safety with LSTM-based Vehicle Intention Prediction (HVIP)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Predicting vehicles' motion on highways has become crucial for enhancing road safety and traffic flow. Deep learning, which reached exceptional results in various applications, is now the leading approach for vehicle motion prediction. This work presents a deep learning-based model using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to classify vehicle intentions into lane-keeping, left lane-changing, and right lane-changing. Utilizing the PREVENTION dataset, which provides naturalistic driving data, a sequence of centre points, longitudinal distances, lateral distances and yaw angles of a vehicle has been extracted to train the model to predict lane changes effectively. The model consists of three LSTM layers, a dense output layer and a drop out added between layers to prevent overfitting. Experiments focusing on optimizing the model parameters, learning rate, sequence length, and batch size, were conducted to determine their impact on prediction effectiveness. The best-performing model showed significant results in lane changing prediction, achieving an accuracy of 84%, precision of 89%, and recall of 82%. Future work will aim to train the model on more complex features, to account for vehicle inter-dependencies and interactions, and test model on various highway scenarios for a more reliable system.

articleTitle: Resilience of Aviation Cyber-Physical Systems to Malicious Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: The inter-connectivity of critical aviation operations are the prime targets for Advance Persistent Threats (APTs) and others malicious actors due to increasingly relying on the Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS). This paper examines the current cyber resilience of aviation CPS to such cyber threats, emerging trends, and proposing new and effective resilience strategies. Using a multi-pronged approach, data were collected through survey from the aviation professionals in the state of Qatar. Quantitative analysis was conducted on survey data to assess trends in threat perception and resilience measures, while qualitative analysis of interviews provided in-depth insights into current vulnerabilities and effective mitigation strategies show that outdated software, insufficient access controls, and complex supply chains increase the risk to advanced persistent threats (APTs) and other sophisticated attacks. Our findings can assist the industry leaders, policymakers, and cybersecurity professionals to get valuable insights to safeguard the aviation ecosystem against the growing cyber threats.

articleTitle: Neurophisology Biosignals of Cognitive Training Classification in Virtual Reality Environment Using Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: This research investigates the potential of neurophysiological biosignals fusion, such as electroencephalogram (EEG) and Eye Tracking signals (ET), to classify cognitive states during virtual reality (VR) training, specifically for the rehabilitation of neurodegenerative diseases. By analyzing EEG data collected from participants engaged in VR-based cognitive exercises, we aim to identify patterns associated with different cognitive states and develop a robust classification system. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model was developed to predict task performance utilizing neurophysiological inputs in an immersive world. This system could be used to monitor cognitive function, assess treatment efficacy, and provide real-time feedback to adapt the VR environment to the individual's needs. The findings of this study could contribute to the development of personalized VR-based rehabilitation programs for neurodegenerative diseases, leading to improved outcomes for patients. The preliminary results of this framework were promising with an overall accuracy of 97% and an average precision of 96.7%.

articleTitle: Enhancing Lung Cancer Classification with MobileNetV3 and EfficientNetB7: A Transfer Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Lung cancer presents a major global health challenge, requiring swift and precise detection for effective treatment. This study examined the effectiveness of six transfer learning models-MobileNetV3, DenseNet201, EfficientNetB7, VGG16, VGG19, and Inception V3-using histopathological images. The dataset included 15,000 images of various lung cancer types, aiming to categorize them into adenocarcinoma, benign, or squamous cell carcinoma. Metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score were used for evaluation. MobileNetV3 achieved an exceptional accuracy of 99.70%, outperforming Inception V3 (78%), DenseNet201 (93%), VGG16 (99%), VGG19 (98%), and EfficientNetB7 (99.50%). Both MobileNetV3 and EfficientNetB7 excelled in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1- score. Therefore, this study recommends MobileNetV3 and Effi- cientNetB7 for lung cancer classification. The proposed method demonstrated significant accuracy, underscoring its effectiveness and practical use. Key model features showed robust precision, recall, and F1-score metrics at 100%, 99%, and 100%, respectively the highest among the models compared. The study also developed a Streamlit-based web application for users to upload images for lung cancer prediction. This research adds to the existing literature by offering a comprehensive approach to early- stage lung cancer detection, addressing previous study limitations and current knowledge gaps.

articleTitle: Analyzing use Intention of LMS in Higher Education: ECM with User Interface Visual Design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: This study evaluates the predictors of LMS usage intentions in higher learning institutions focusing on ECM and Interface Visual Design. The use of the internet and technology has developed tremendously and education has gone from traditional education to e-learning through LMS. These changes bring questions on user acquisition and usage which is a call for factors of influence of the users. The research employs ECM which consists of perceived usefulness, perceived satisfaction, perceived confirmation, continuance intention and the moderating role of visual design on user satisfaction. The work collects data from 110 respondents that are students and lecturers from Higher education in Jabodetabek region who engage in LMS. Using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), the study finds that perceived usefulness, confirmation, and satisfaction are significant predictors of LMS continuance usage intention. However, visual design did not significantly influence user satisfaction which means that usability and the function of features in LMS are more critical than visual design in driving the satisfaction that led to user continuance usage. Therefore, it is recommended for future researchers as well as LMS developers to provide perceptions of usefulness and confirmation to enhance usage and user satisfaction for effective learning. Such findings could be useful for the improved architecture of LMS platforms to increase their usability with students in higher learning institutions.

articleTitle: Real-Time Cloud-based Data Analysis Using Machine Learning for Smart Parking
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: The fourth industrial revolution has led to the emergence of smart cities and intelligent transportation systems that rely heavily on large-scale data-driven models. One of the most popular applications of these models is smart parking, which has gained significant attention from both researchers and industry professionals. However, different scenarios and environments require different approaches due to the various factors that can impact people's schedules and behavior. This paper aims to investigate traffic assignments based on parking prediction for a mid-size university environment with multiple parking garages around the campus and various types of permits in each garage. The investigation involves utilizing multiple machine learning (ML) techniques to predict parking garage correlation. To achieve this, we collected data from different parking garages and used some of this data to train our ML algorithm. The machine learning models developed in this study demonstrated significant predictive accuracy. Our baseline model achieved an RMSE of 33.15, whereas our enhanced model incorporating features like availability ratio and other temporal features reduced the RMSE to 0.0864, with near-perfect prediction accuracy (MAPE < 0.005%). These results underscore the effectiveness of feature engineering and advanced modeling in addressing the complexities of parking availability prediction.

articleTitle: A Methodology to Convert Tacit Knowledge into Explicit Knowledge - Smart Building Use Case
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Managing energy in smart buildings involves complex interactions best understood by domain experts. This work introduces the Tacit Knowledge Tree (TKT) methodology, which is a 4-stage framework to capture and structure tacit knowledge into semi-structured formats. TKT maps causal relationships of events to enhance cyber-physical system explainability and decision-making. TKT has been applied to a smart building use case for evaluation.

articleTitle: Epistemological Advancements in Cardiological Forecasting: Machine Learning as a Paradigm for Prognostic Precision
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) constitutes a heterogeneous ensemble of pathological conditions impacting the heart and vasculature, encompassing a multitude of disorders within the cardiovascular apparatus. Among these, heart failure (HF) emerges as a particularly pervasive and deleterious malady, afflicting individuals across all demographic strata. HF ensues when the myocardium is incapable of propelling blood with requisite efficacy, precipitating manifestations such as dyspnea, lassitude, and fluid retention. This insidious, progressive affliction substantially exacerbates mortality risk, particularly in the presence of concomitant comorbidities. For clinicians, prognosticating survival probabilities for HF patients remains a formidable challenge, necessitating the deployment of computational methodologies to enable nuanced and expeditious therapeutic determinations. Machine learning (ML) algorithms proffer an avant-garde paradigm, empowering cardiologists to devise bespoke treatment regimens derived from pertinent clinical data. This investigation endeavors to construct an interpretable ML-driven prognostic framework for HF survival analysis. Leveraging the UCI HF dataset, comprising clinical records of numerous patients, we undertook rigorous data curation and preprocessing to refine data integrity and elucidate distributional properties. Essential procedures, including meticulous data cleaning and feature engineering, were employed to bolster predictive precision. The study assessed an array of ML algorithms—Naïve Bayes (NB), Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost (XGB), and LightGBM—while employing hyperparameter optimization and overfitting mitigation strategies to enhance model robustness. Evaluation metrics such as precision, recall, F1-score, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were prioritized to furnish a comprehensive appraisal, transcending reliance on accuracy alone. Empirical findings revealed the preeminence of the Random Forest (RF) classifier, which achieved an accuracy of 87.77% and an AUC of 94.36% in forecasting HF patient survival. These outcomes illuminate the transformative potential of ML methodologies in refining clinical prognostication, equipping cardiologists with actionable intelligence to enact prompt and informed clinical interventions, thereby augmenting patient care and prognostic precision.

articleTitle: Fine-Tuning an Arabic OCR Model using Tesseract 5.0
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is a crucial technology for the digital processing and preservation of textual information. While significant progress has been made in OCR for commonly used languages, the recognition of Arabic script poses unique challenges due to its complex linguistic characteristics. This research paper presents a comprehensive approach to collecting data and training an Arabic OCR system using the latest version of the Tesseract OCR engine. Integrating the customized Tesseract model, the study achieved high accuracy in text recognition, as measured by character error rate (CER) and word error rate (WER). The findings highlight the complexities of the Arabic language, including diacritics and ligatures, and discuss the limitations of the current approach. This study contributes to the advancement of optical character recognition, providing a robust Arabic OCR solution that can be leveraged in various applications, from digitizing historical documents to automating text extraction.

articleTitle: Analyzing Neuroimaging Epiphenomena: Machine Learning Approaches in Alzheimer's Prognostication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) constitutes a progressive neurodegenerative pathology that undermines cognitive faculties, mnemonic capacity, and the aptitude for executing quotidian tasks in geriatric individuals, frequently accompanied by alterations in demeanor and temperament. In the absence of a definitive cure, extant therapeutic interventions demonstrate optimal efficacy during the initial and intermediary phases of AD, underscoring the criticality of precocious diagnosis amidst the burgeoning geriatric demographic and the concomitant escalation in AD prevalence. This inquiry endeavors to discern incipient indicators of AD by harnessing machine learning and deep learning methodologies to scrutinize MRI imagery derived from the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS) dataset. A spectrum of algorithms was deployed, encompassing Random Forest and Logistic Regression within traditional machine learning paradigms, Extra Trees as an exemplar of ensemble learning, and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) representative of deep learning architectures. The efficacy of these models was appraised through metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and area under the curve (AUC), wherein CNN exhibited preeminent accuracy and AUC metrics, while Extra Trees distinguished itself in precision and recall, substantiating the capacity of both deep learning and ensemble learning modalities to deliver robust performance in the early detection of AD.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Security and Privacy Challenges of IoT Devices in the Hotels Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: The rapid proliferation of IoT devices has revolutionized the hospitality industry, offering enhanced guest experiences and operational efficiencies. However, this adoption introduces significant cybersecurity challenges, risking guest privacy and data integrity. This study is a solemn attempt evaluates the current state of IoT device deployment and challenges in hotels, identifies common vulnerabilities, and proposes a general framework to manage these devices and encourages the hotel guest to use them. Researcher designed different questionnaires for guest, front-end and back-end staffs to address the IoT challenges efficiently. Researcher collected 109 responses from the hotel quests and analyzed them. Interviews with hotels staff have been also conducted to further improve the proposed framework that should be adapted in hotels to provide more comfort for the guests.

articleTitle: Enabling Unified and Scalable IoT Ecosystems: A Customisable Data Framework for Interoperability Across Heterogeneous Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Managing the growing diversity of IoT devices and data formats presents significant challenges for integration and consistency within interconnected ecosystems. To address these, we propose a customizable JSON framework for unified data representation, enabling seamless communication between heterogeneous devices and IoT platforms. The framework defines a flexible JSON grammar that encapsulates device-specific attributes and metadata, ensuring interoperability and consistency. Devices communicate either directly or via gateways, with the structured data transmitted to a modular Data Collection Platform (DCP). The DCP validates and organizes the data for database integration, supporting dynamic adaptability to new device types and sensor inputs with minimal reconfiguration. Our experiments across domains such as environmental monitoring, industrial automation, automotive telematics, and smart home systems highlight the framework's ability to simplify data representation while maintaining consistency across platforms. By standardizing data formats, the framework enhances ease-of-use for analytics tools, enabling seamless interpretation and application of insights across diverse use cases. This paper presents a detailed implementation of the JSON framework and its architecture, emphasizing its ability to address device heterogeneity, ensure interoperability, and provide a consistent foundation for scalable IoT ecosystems.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Secure Real-Time Multimedia Surveillance Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Multimedia management systems handle sensitive data in various applications such as surveillance, health care, and insurance. However, current multimedia surveillance systems face many challenges in ensuring the integrity, confidentiality, and privacy of sensitive data in transit and at rest. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an extensible framework that combines blockchain technology and end-to-end encryption to create a secure, tamper-proof, and decentralized multimedia surveillance system capable of supporting time-sensitive multimedia data processing and transmission requirements. The primary objective of the proposed framework is to highly secure the transmission of multimedia data by developing a robust and scalable architecture that can effectively manage and protect the transmission of multimedia-sensitive data. In addition, it provides a secure decentralized data warehouse for storage and verification of data integrity and confidentiality. Analytical analysis illustrates the feasibility of the proposed framework in terms of the calculated number of cryptographic operations and scalability. In addition, an initial proof-of-concept implementation demonstrates the overhead time involved in storing and retrieving an event of interest within a blockchain.

articleTitle: Safeguarding Virtual Healthcare: A Novel Attacker-Centric Model for Data Security and Privacy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: The rapid growth of remote healthcare delivery has introduced significant security and privacy risks to protected health information (PHI). Analysis of a comprehensive healthcare security breach dataset covering 2009–2023 reveals their significant prevalence and impact. This study investigates the root causes of such security incidents and introduces the Attacker-Centric Approach (ACA), a novel threat model tailored to protect PHI. ACA addresses limitations in existing threat models and regulatory frameworks by adopting a holistic attacker-focused perspective, examining threats from the viewpoint of cyber adversaries, their motivations, tactics, and potential attack vectors. Leveraging established risk management frameworks, ACA provides a multi-layered approach to threat identification, risk assessment, and proactive mitigation strategies. A comprehensive threat library classifies physical, third-party, external, and internal threats. ACA's iterative nature and feedback mechanisms enable continuous adaptation to emerging threats, ensuring sustained effectiveness. ACA allows healthcare providers to proactively identify and mitigate vulnerabilities, fostering trust and supporting the secure adoption of virtual care technologies.

articleTitle: Hybrid zk-STARK and zk-SNARK Framework for Privacy-Preserving Smart Contract Data Feeds
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Decentralized applications (DApps) are increasingly using off-chain data, yet growing concerns about data privacy hinder their widespread adoption. Zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) have emerged as a solution to this problem. This paper proposes a novel hybrid framework that combines Zero-Knowledge Scalable Transparent Arguments of Knowledge (zk-STARKs) and Zero-Knowledge Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments of Knowledge (zk-SNARKs) to deliver an efficient, scalable, quantum-resistant, and privacy-preserving ZKP system. The framework employs zk-STARKs' ability to handle large computations with quantum resistance and zk-SNARKs' succinct proofs and fast verification. The hybrid framework utilizes advanced arithmetization techniques to balance scalability, privacy, and security, including Algebraic Intermediate Representation (AIR) for zk-STARKs and Rank-1 Constraint Systems (RlCS) or PLONKish constraints for zk-SNARKs. The framework uses the Kate-Zaverucha-Goldberg (KZG) polynomial commitment scheme for reliability and transparency and eliminates trusted setup by using Discrete-logarithm-based Argument of Recursive Knowledge (DARK) commitments and Poseidon hashing. This paper details the construction of the hybrid proof system, analyzes its complexity, and explores its potential applications. The framework solves smart contract data feed limitations, security, efficiency, and scalability while prioritizing privacy.

articleTitle: Artistic Style Classification using Convolution Sparse Coding
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Artistic style classification is an important part of visual artwork study. This paper describes a new approach for enhancing the accuracy of artist classification for line drawing images. We rely on the use of convolutional sparse coding that is known for its ability to model artistic styles through convolutional dictionary elements that represent artist brush strokes. We evaluate this framework by using two different datasets formed of various line drawing images generated by multiple artists where each artist owns a different artistic style. Once the dataset is prepared, it is preprocessed, and then used to train a convolutional sparse coding model to distinguish the artistic styles. This facilitates the process of discriminative feature learning of artistic styles by relying on the process of convolutional dictionary learning. The experimental results show that our approach outperforms other alternatives and guarantees significant progress for enhancing the field of artist style classification.

articleTitle: Roadmap of AIoT Implementation on Sustainable SCM in the Food Industry: A Requirements Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: One of the most vital challenges faced by the human population is transforming all the procedures conducted in businesses and human consumption of natural resources methods into sustainable methods that preserve the environment. The interconnection of the organizations involved in the supply chain, provided by Supply Chain Management (SCM), is included in one of the demanding practices necessitating the sustainability transformation due to its harmful impact on the environment. To reach the goal of sustain ability transformation, the use of smart technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT), is a prerequisite [14]. This paper aims to explore the effect of AIoT technologies on Sustainable Food Supply Chain Management, including the opportunities and challenges of such implementation. The scientific approach used in the thesis paper is a literature review method. The food SCM was investigated as these types of systems had a specific set of requirements and needs, resulting in the creation of a requirements framework.

articleTitle: Split-Federated Reinforcement Learning for IoMT Data and Task Management in Edge-Fog-Cloud Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Workload management in edge-fog-cloud infrastructure for the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) involves significant costs and difficulties, primarily due to the challenge of managing tasks and the unpredictability of data generated by IoMT devices while processing real-time patient health states. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) shows promise in efficiently addressing dynamic data placement and task offloading. However, DRL suffers from poor scalability in distributed multi-node IoT environments. To address these challenges, Federated Learning (FL) and DRL are combined to provide potential solutions, but they face coordination complexities, privacy concerns, high computational and communication costs, and scalability issues. In this paper, a new solution called Split Federated Hybrid Decision-based DRL (SF-HDRL) is introduced to tackle these challenges. Our algorithm combines continuous and discrete actions within a splitting actor-critic architecture to achieve joint optimized data placement, as well as node selection for task execution, while minimizing IoMT operational costs. Simulations indicate that the proposed SF-HDRL algorithm is superior in scalability and workload management costs compared to existing optimal non-federated and federated approaches.

articleTitle: Pre-Programmable Directional Stiffness in Continuum Robotic Arms: Effects of Truss Configurations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: This paper investigates the implementation of trussed designs in modular tendon-driven continuum arms (CAs) to address stiffness and stability limitations while maintaining adaptability. Various truss configurations-Single-Level, Combined-Level, and Alternated trusses-were analyzed using Finite Element Analysis (FEA) to evaluate their impact on flexural and axial stiffness under realistic loading conditions. Results demonstrate that truss placement significantly influences performance, with bottom-level trusses improving flexural stiffness by up to 33 %, middle-level trusses enhancing axial stiffness by 43%. Further, Combined-Level configurations provide superior overall stiffness, with Middle-Bottom trusses achieving a 66.5% improvement in flexural stiffness and a 70.9% increase in axial stiffness, while fully trussed configurations maximize rigidity with an 87.8% increase in flexural stiffness and 98.5% in axial stiffness. Alternated configurations achieve anisotropic stiffness for directional control. Additionally, the proposed trussed wing approach enhances stiffness programmability with reduced complexity, eliminating the need for full segment disassembly or tendon re-routing. The proposed trussed CAs enable tailored stiffness and directional control in robotics, medical devices, and aerospace systems.

articleTitle: Evaluating Explainability in XAI: A Case Study of Bug Assignment and Developer Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has gained significant importance in software engineering, especially in tasks like bug assignment and developer allocation, which require trust and transparency. However, what constitutes a satisfactory explanation is difficult to determine because user satisfaction may be subjective and stakeholder expectations may differ. This paper provides a quality evaluation framework for explain ability, applied to bug assignment and developer allocation. It further categorizes into multiple dimensions, such as transparency, interpretability, and satisfaction of users, tailored to the needs of software development teams. We propose a framework to evaluate which types of explanations are helpful and assign weights to various criteria with respect to their introduction into the development process. The proposed framework supports assessing whether the XAI system improves decision-making support as intended. We illustrate the application of our framework in real-world scenarios through case studies and empirical analysis, providing guidance on how to maximize trust in XAI systems while also improving efficiency in software development workflows.

articleTitle: Virtual Restaurant Platform Based on AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Restaurants are progressively utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) to alleviate and resolve the persistent challenges of protracted wait times, manufacturing errors, supply chain complications, and labor shortages. Although the standard understanding of artificial intelligence in restaurants sets up images of kitchens staffed by machines that have been instructed, this does not accurately represent the technology's actuality. The most common ways in which artificial intelligence is impacting restaurant operations are by reducing the number of errors caused by humans, managing increasing expenses, improving production accuracy, adhering to safety regulations, and redefining the customer experience within the restaurant. Restaurant owners and administrators can take advantage from artificial intelligence procedures that are designed to enhance capacity, enhance forecasting precision, and expedite production while concurrently stimulating development. Additionally, devices that are equipped with virtual assistants and artificial intelligence may be assigned the responsibility of effectively managing client conversations, reservations, and suggestions, in addition to providing customized ordering. This paper offers a comprehensive examination of the methods that have been employed to integrate AI into virtual restaurant platforms, and is dedicated to the development of an intelligent customer order management platform that efficiently streamlines the order process by utilizing AI technology. The paper illustrates the proposed virtual restaurant platform that is based on AI, and explains its distinct features and functions. The proposed virtual restaurant platform is designed with the objective of enhancing the customer ordering experience, enabling customers to personalize their chosen meals, and enhancing the operational efficiency of restaurants.

articleTitle: AdaptVR: An Adaptive Learning VR System for Dental Students Training
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: The paper proposes “AdaptVR” a virtual reality (VR) system designed to enhance dental training through realistic real tile simulations and adaptive learning environment, to overcome traditional training challenges in dental education. The system aims to provide personalized learning experiences, facilitating skill development and comprehensive assessments for students. The proposed system was tested by 17 dentistry students and 5 experts. AdaptVR framework is done for operative dentistry which is removing decay especially Class I and Class II of classification of caries. Results from the experiment revealed that 77.3% of participants exceed their expectations, 59.1% saw a positive effect on their dental skills, 90.9% reported higher levels of engagement, and 65% indicated that vibration and force feedback provided students with a genuine sensation. AdpatVR's experimental findings show an average accuracy of 50.85% for Class I, 51.7% for Class II, and 82.09% for the Class II box technique. The error percentage averages 49% for Class I, 48% for Class II, and 18% for Class II box technique.

articleTitle: A Survey of Clustering Algorithms for Self-Reconfiguration on Programmable Matter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Self-reconfiguration is a challenge for the deployment of modular robotics. Building a large number of self-configurable robots consisting of a bunch of modules is the ideal approach to implement programmable matter. The latter is a set of particles or modules that combine to form a desired object. It is composed of a set of micro-robots, mobile computers of millimetric size that will have the ability to move around each other, communicate, change colors and lock on other micro-robots to form different shapes. It is applied in several fields such as surgery, construction, nuclear, environment, … These particles are deployed in unmonitored environments, or the modules cannot be charged, so size and energy constraints are the most critical issues to consider before deploying the system. Clustering modules in modular robots is a challenge to facilitate self-reconfiguration. Self-configuration clustering algorithms are used to overcome communication problems, energy limits, aggregation modules during auto-configuration. In this paper, after reviewing clustering algorithms in sensor networks and graphs, we study self-configuration based on clustering algorithms for existing modular robot systems. After a comparative study of algorithms, the proposed solutions try to facilitate communication, reduce execution time and the number of messages exchanged during the self-configuration process.

articleTitle: Scrappy City: A Waste Management Simulation Video Game Promoting Environmental Awareness
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: “Scrappy City” is an innovative 2D waste management simulation video game designed to promote environmental awareness among young adults and teenagers. Developed using the Unity Game Engine, this Android-based mobile application gamifies waste management education, offering an engaging platform for learning about proper waste disposal practices and environmental stewardship. The game incorporates key features such as an open-world environment, educational non-playable characters, and a progressive star system to unlock new areas. The implementation leverages three core algorithms: NPCs utilize Decision-Tree Logic for dynamic interaction and mission management, achieving 98.5% dialogue path accuracy; the inventory system employs a hashmap with stacking and counting algorithm for waste categorization, demonstrating an F1 score of 0.935; and a state-based check algorithm underpins the achievement system, maintaining 99.7% state tracking accuracy with an F1 score of 0.979. This study uses the ISO 25010:2023 software quality model to evaluate the game's effectiveness, focusing on functional suitability, performance efficiency, interaction capability, reliability, and security. Results from a survey of 100 participants across diverse age groups and occupations demonstrate exceptionally positive reception, with all evaluated criteria receiving “Excellent” ratings. Technical performance analysis shows response times averaging under 150ms across all systems, with memory usage optimized for mobile devices. The game's usability, performance metrics, and educational value were particularly praised, indicating its potential as a powerful tool for environmental education. This research contributes to the growing field of serious games for education, offering insights into effective design strategies and algorithm implementation for environmental awareness games.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approach to Predict Student Performance Based on Previous Records
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Educational Data Mining (EDM) is an emerging field dedicated to discovering and analyzing meaningful patterns in educational datasets. This paper provides a comparative analysis of seven machine-learning classifiers: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Naive Bayes (NB), and Neural Network (NN). The primary objective is to evaluate these algorithms, combined with preprocessing techniques, for predicting student performance and identifying the most effective classifier using metrics such as the confusion matrix, accuracy, precision, and sensitivity. The dataset utilized in this study was obtained from Sebha University, Libya, comprising 6,000 student records. It includes 6 attributes from the university's SIS system and 43 attributes derived from completed questionnaires, focusing exclusively on students from scientific departments. The experimental results revealed that the RF algorithm outperformed other classifiers in predicting student performance. Significant improvements in the model's performance were observed after applying data preprocessing and feature selection techniques. These findings offer valuable insights to help new students select suitable academic programs, potentially enhancing their academic performance. Furthermore, the proposed model could serve as an early warning system to identify students at risk of academic failure, enabling timely intervention.

articleTitle: The Application of Virtual Fencing in Home Security Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: To increase the security of homes and bring relief to homeowners when they are away from it, Security Systems that may be able to perform real-time monitoring and detection of intruders breaching the bounds of their property could be solved by implementing the concept of Virtual Fences in Computer Vision using Machine Learning. This paper covers previous implementations of Virtual Fencing while emphasizing Object Detection methods that are required to perform such a task. Explores the dichotomy between single stage and two stage detectors and compares their architecture, performance, and applications. It examines various datasets that may be used to train object detection models and performance metrics that could be used to analyse and benchmark the capabilities of such models. A proof of concept is developed using the YOLOv8 model and a custom Virtual Fencing Logic along with a comparison between performance of YOLOv8 and YOLOv9 variants.

articleTitle: Beyond RGB: Channel Fusion for Improved Cross-Domain Car Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Domain adaptation in cross-domain vision has significantly improved detection performance under adverse weather and visibility conditions. However, this enhancement has come at the cost of substantial complexity in the training routine and an increase in computational cost. In this article; a crossdomain car detection framework is proposed that outperforms state-of-the-art domain-adaptive detectors while maintaining a remarkably lower model complexity and computational overhead. The proposed model architecture is based on YOLOv8 with the integration of CBAM (Convolutional Block Attention Module). In addition, a novel channel combination is proposed where the ‘Y’(Luminance) channel from the YCbCr color space is fused with the ‘G’(Green) and ‘B’(Blue) channels from the RGB color space producing YGB. The BDD100K data set is used for model training and validation to adapt the model to a driving context where it can be deployed in autonomous cars. The proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art models in cross-domain car detection by at least 3.95 % in precision, and at least 11.81 % in F1 score. When compared to other equally performing state-of-the-art domain adaptation techniques, it showed drastic decrease in the number of trainable parameters (up to 95.2%).

articleTitle: Exploring the Role of Digital Financial Tools in Personal Finance: Enhancing Financial Planning and Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: In this research, we propose an advanced monthly budget planner that leverages historical financial data to predict future budgeting needs across four main components: income, investments, expenditure, and tax management. The features of our system imply that machine learning is used to find patterns and trends from previous data and give the users proper financial advice. The planner takes information from income variability, investment earnings, fixed and variable expenses, and tax liability, and provides in return a budget plan and possible strategies for saving and spending for the subsequent thirty days. Furthermore, the system includes promotional analysis for basket analysis so that the users can get shopping suggestions and the most amount of money can be saved. Its integrated approach helps people to develop sound financial plans, manage their budgets effectively, and financially prosper.

articleTitle: Enhancing Adherence and Completion Rates Through Gamification and Micro AI Interventions in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: In the contemporary digital era, mental health awareness has improved, yet challenges remain in therapy adherence and social stigma associated with seeking help for mental disorders such as depression, anxiety, and PTSD. Premature discontinuation of psychological therapies is prevalent, particularly among younger demographics like millennials and Generation Z, who often face significant societal judgment. This research paper presents a computer science project that explores the potential of gamification and micro-AI to enhance retention and completion rates in cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT). The project develops an interactive application that employs gamification strategies to increase engagement and motivation in therapy sessions. Additionally, it integrates micro-AI for real-time mood analysis, offering personalized feedback and support, thereby deepening users' connection to the therapeutic process. With functional testing pass rate of 94%, the primary goal of this innovation is to improve mental health outcomes by mitigating the issues of adherence and premature therapy dropout, providing a scalable and technologically integrated approach to mental health interventions. This study evaluates the effectiveness of these interventions through quantitative metrics and user feedback, aiming to contribute valuable insights into the intersection of technology and mental health.

articleTitle: A Review of Super Resolution Technology for Extended-Range Precipitation Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: In the field of meteorology, precipitation holds significant importance for human activities and environment. Extended-range precipitation forecasting, covering a timeframe of weeks to months, is crucial across various sectors, including water resource management, agriculture, and disaster prevention. However, the conventional meteorological forecasting models often fail to satisfy the precise demand for accurate and detailed precipitation predictions due to the inherent limitations in resolution and data collection frequency associated with these methods. Recently, super resolution technology has emerged as a promising solution with the potential to transform the resolution of meteorological data. By leveraging advanced algorithms and computational prowess, this technology can generate high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs. In this comprehensive review, we meticulously dissect the state-of-the-art super resolution techniques utilized in extended-range precipitation forecasting tasks. By classifying and analyzing the literature based on various methodologies, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), generative adversarial networks (GANs), and diffusion models, we uncover their performance characteristics, strengths, and limitations. Our in-depth exploration reveals that while these methods have shown promise, they also face significant challenges. For example, CNNs struggle with capturing ultrafine details, GANs exhibit training instability, and diffusion models require further optimizations in terms of their computational efficiency. Future research efforts should focus on enhancing model architectures, seamlessly incorporating physical constraints to ensure the physical consistency of the generated data, and optimizing the current data utilization strategies. Furthermore, it is crucial to develop comprehensive evaluation metrics, conduct extensive long-term and regional validation studies, and establish effective uncertainty quantification methods. Additionally, the seamless integration of super resolution forecasts into practical applications such as decision support systems for flood prevention and water resource management, as well as their applications in climate change studies, will be pivotal for unlocking the full potential of this technology and addressing the longstanding challenges faces in precipitation forecasting scenarios.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Forecasting of Smart Grid Stability Using Advanced Deep Learning and Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: This study comprehensively examines the ability to forecast the stability of smart grids using sophisticated deep learning and machine learning models. We investigate different approaches, such as Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU), Multi-Layer Perceptron with Extreme Learning Machine (MLP-ELM), and innovative fusion models that combine Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) with Support Vector Machines (SVM). The performance of these models was evaluated by comparing parameters such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F-measure. The dataset is an improved version of the Electrical Grid Stability Simulated Dataset from the Karlsruher Institut für Technologie. It consists of 60,000 observations and includes twelve primary prediction variables. Before training and testing the models, we conducted thorough exploratory data analysis (EDA) and preprocessing. The solution we present utilizes a Sequential model that incorporates multiple optimizers and activation functions. This approach achieves a maximum accuracy of 99.48% when using the Adamax optimizer. The results indicate the substantial capacity of deep learning methods to improve the dependability and effectiveness of smart grid stability forecasts. This work offers a novel deep learning methodology for predicting the stability of smart grids, attaining a prediction accuracy of 99.48 % and exhibiting enhanced performance relative to leading methodologies. Comprehensive testing across several grid settings demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed tactics, rendering it very beneficial for real-time stability forecasts.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Skin Disease Identification Using Augmented Data and Transfer Learning: Achieving Optimal Accuracy with Sequential Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Skin diseases are a significant global concern, and effectively treating bacterial and fungal skin infections poses an enormous task. Furthermore, in more severe instances, it might occasionally result in a case of skin cancer. Diagnosing skin diseases from clinical photographs is challenging in medical image analysis. In addition, the process of diagnosing skin issues manually by medical professionals is both time-consuming and subjective. In this work, Deep learning and machine learning-based model has been designed for the identification of skin disease using the concept of transfer learning. For this, the VGG16 model, sequential, KNN, logistic regression, and decision tree classifiers are used. VGG16's basic architecture comprises 16 weight layers, with 13 convolutional and 3 completely linked. Because ability to accurately extract complex features from skin photos is a result of its simplicity and depth. The model's ability to generalize is enhanced by its pretrained training on huge image datasets such as ImageNet. Excellent performance with little medical data can be achieved by fine-tuning this pretrained model on specific skin disease datasets. Improving patient outcomes can be achieved through earlier diagnosis and treatment, which is made possible by its ability to detect subtle patterns and early indicators of skin illnesses that may not be visible to the human eye. These proposed models are evaluated on three datasets obtained from Kaggle. These datasets now include 246 of our own captured images, which are added as healthy classes. Data augmentation techniques are used to improve the randomness of the input dataset in order to ensure model stability. The sequential model works best with an overall accuracy of 96% with the Adam optimizer and 10 epochs, outperforming state-of-the-art techniques. This model will help dermatologists diagnose skin diseases early.

articleTitle: Protein-Protein Interaction Sites Prediction Using Graph Convolutional Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPI) are essential in keeping the cells functioning properly. Identifying PPI binding sites is a fundamental problem in system Biology, and it contributes to a better understanding of lower organisms such as viruses, a multitude-drug design and vaccines. The experimental methods for PPI binding sites identification are slow and expensive. Therefore, great research efforts have been attempted to improve the performance of computational methods. In this paper, we use a deep learning model based on Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) to predict putative interaction sites on the surface of an isolated protein. We extracted features from both protein sequence and structure to enhance the accuracy of PPI binding sites predictions. Our model achieved higher accuracy compared to other models.

articleTitle: Advanced Arabic Alphabet Sign Language Recognition Using Transfer Learning and Transformer Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: This paper presents an Arabic Alphabet Sign Language recognition approach, using deep learning methods in conjunction with transfer learning and transformer-based models. We study the performance of the different variants on two publicly available datasets, namely ArSL2018 and AASL. This task will make full use of state-of-the-art CNN architectures like ResNet50, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB7, and the latest transformer models such as Google ViT and Microsoft Swin Transformer. These pre-trained models have been fine-tuned on the above datasets in an attempt to capture some unique features of Arabic sign language motions. Experimental results present evidence that the suggested methodology can receive a high recognition accuracy, by up to 99.6% and 99.43% on ArSL2018 and AASL, respectively. That is far beyond the previously reported state-of-the-art approaches. This performance opens up even more avenues for communication that may be more accessible to Arabic-speaking deaf and hard-of-hearing, and thus encourages an inclusive society.

articleTitle: PRINIA: Privacy-Preserving Facial Recognition Framework for Extended Reality Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Face recognition technology's integration into Extended Reality (XR) environments offers new opportunities but raises significant privacy and data protection concerns. Therefore, there is a critical need to develop privacy-preserving facial recognition solutions for XR applications that comply with data protection regulations. To address this challenge, we propose the PRINIA framework, which implements facial recognition in XR environments while safeguarding individuals' privacy and personal data. PRINIA is autonomous and compatible with broader technological frameworks like SERMAS, covering various XR scenarios, such as identifying users of head-mounted displays (HMDs), recognizing people in XR environments, and classifying individuals based on facial characteristics analysis.

articleTitle: Detecting Fraud in Food Delivery: Leveraging Amazon Web Services' Random Cut Forest and XGBoost Models for Enhanced Security
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: This paper introduces a fraud detection model tailored for identifying fraudulent cases and anomalies within business systems. Choosing the multivariate Random Cut Forest over the univariate Isolation Forest, the model demonstrated effectiveness in detecting various anomalies and ensuring system safety. Evaluated with a limited set of confirmed fraud cases, it achieved significant results with a cutoff score of 1.4, effectively identifying instances resembling known fraud cases and flagging anomalies for further investigation. These findings refined engine rules, enhancing system security and stability. The model, leveraging XGBoost for its proficiency with complex datasets and multivariate features, integrates parameters like price, delivery fee, discounts, cash back value, and distance metrics. Notably, the models achieved strong performance, with the food model scoring 0.816 and the on-demand model 0.790 in test F1 scores. Deployment involves storing models in an S3 bucket, deploying them in SageMaker endpoints using XGBoost version 1.0-1 and ml.t2.medium instance type, with weekly re-training and deployment schedules and daily dataset updates. An AWS Lambda function ensures efficient inference processing via the API. Overall, this study contributes a versatile and efficient fraud detection model for enhancing business system security and stability.

articleTitle: A Contextualized Deep Neural Network Model for Classifying IT Incidents Based on Severity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: IT service management operational efficiency is significantly dependent on the accuracy and cost of IT tickets classification. Whilst several machine learning techniques have made significant progress in the task of IT tickets classification, Classifying tickets by severity remains inherently complex, costly and multifaceted. It requires a deep understanding and interpretation of contextual information in words, phrases, and sentences. Additionally, the correlation between the classification process and operational costs impacts the efficacy and effectiveness of IT operations. This paper introduces the Severity Misclassification Impact (SMI) as a novel metric of quantifying the operational costs of misclassification errors by accounting for the varying costs associated with the different types of errors due to misclassifications. To highlight the need for SMI in contextual classification, this paper proposes a novel blended model approach comprising Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), Term Frequency-inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LightGBM). By conducting extensive experiments on real-world IT Tickets, it demonstrates that incorporating SMI as an evaluation metric enables a robust way to assess a classification model's potential. This approach offers a nuanced understanding of its effectiveness in minimizing operational costs of misclassification, hence significantly improving IT tickets classification.

articleTitle: Advancements in Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques for Sickle Cell Disease Detection using Digital Morphology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) is still a serious public health concern, particularly in areas with inadequate access to healthcare. The management of the condition depends on an early and precise diagnosis; yet, traditional diagnostic techniques, such manual blood smear examinations, are frequently laborious, subjective, and prone to variability. The major developments in deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML) approaches that are redefining SCD detection especially with regard to the application of digital morphology are examined in this review paper. The sickle-shaped red blood cells from microscopic pictures can effectively categorized by utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs), transfer learning, and ensemble learning techniques. This method offers better accuracy, speed, and scalability over conventional approaches. These models allow for more accurate assessments of cell morphology in addition to improving the accuracy of SCD diagnosis, lowering the possibility of human error. Additionally, issues like interpretability and data imbalance, offering answers via creative model designs and pre-processing methods. This research demonstrates the revolutionary potential of machine learning and deep learning in the healthcare industry, where intelligent, automated technologies may supplement clinical knowledge and improve outcomes for SCD patients worldwide. By combining these technologies, scalable and easily available diagnostic tools could be developed in the future, leading to more fair healthcare delivery.

articleTitle: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Quantum Wavefunctions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: The wave functions and permitted energy levels of quantum systems, which characterize the probability distributions and particle behaviors, are able to be determined via the time-independent Schrodinger equation. Our research study introduces an experimental method of solving the time-independent Schrodinger equation by utilizing Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) with a customized loss function designed for output waveshape prediction. The technique makes use of PINNs' capacity to directly integrate physical rules into the learning process, assuring that the solutions follow the guiding principles of quantum mechanics. We forecast the associated wavefunctions for different energy levels (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> states) and effectively solve the Schrodinger equation for distinct quantum states by using PINNs and a customized loss function. Our findings show that PINNs are a reliable and accurate way to represent the fine features of quantum wavefunctions, and they present a viable substitute for more conventional numerical techniques. This methodology not only improves computer performance but also offers more profound understanding of the behavior of systems in quantum mechanics, which may have implications for material science, nanotechnology, and quantum computing.

articleTitle: DenseNet121 with Harris Hawks Optimization: A Novel Deep Learning Approach for Arabic Sign Language Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for Arabic Sign Language (ArSL) recognition by leveraging advanced deep learning models with optimization techniques. Several architectures, including CNNs, EfficientNet, ResNet50, and DenseNet, are evaluated and integrated with Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) to enhance performance. Our DenseNet121 model, optimized with HHO, achieved state-of-the-art accuracy, surpassing previous models. Using the ArASL2018 dataset of 54,049 images, models were evaluated on metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The DenseNet121 and HHO model achieved an impressive 99.79 percent, demonstrating its potential for assistive technologies and human-computer interaction.

articleTitle: Accelerating Systematic Reviews Via Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: An essential part of developing practice guidelines and health policy involves examining the evidence generated by studies published that compare the effect of competing interventions on specific health outcomes. This is achieved through systematic reviews (SRs), which are rigorous reviews of several medical databases, on papers related to the topic of interest, within a specified time interval. However, the process of conducting SRs is labor-intensive and very time-consuming. In this paper, we apply natural language processing (NLP) techniques to enhance the efficiency of selecting relevant medical literature, thereby reducing the time required for researchers to manually screen, select, and review articles and identify relevant ones. The proposed algorithm automates the selection process by comparing titles and abstracts of articles to predefined criteria. If eligible, the article then undergoes full-text screening; otherwise, it is excluded. In the second stage, the full text is scrutinized to extract content that aligns with the intervention(s) and outcome(s) of interest. The proposed automation tool was tested in an umbrella review (SR of systematic reviews) on Vitamin D and falls, demonstrating significant benefit in reducing the time and effort required by researchers. The number of articles to be reviewed was reduced from 17,776 to 188, achieving a 100% recall rate, thus ensuring all relevant articles were included, and a 99% specificity rate, thus successfully excluding most irrelevant articles. This approach also led to a substantial reduction in the screening time, a 13.75 time-gain factor, decreasing the estimated review time from months to years to an estimated of two and a half months.

articleTitle: Integration of Geospatial Analysis for Enhancing Rubber Plantation Management in Sri Lanka
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Rubber cultivation is a significant economic activity in many regions, necessitating precise identification of suitable land for optimal yield. This research paper presents a comprehensive analysis leveraging Geographic Information System (GIS) technology to assess factors such as slope, elevation, soil type, and climatic conditions in determining the suitability of land for rubber cultivation. By categorizing lands into suitable, average, or unsuitable categories, farmers are equipped with vital insights for informed decision-making. Additionally, we employ GIS techniques to map rubber growers and calculate rubber field areas, excluding regions with deserted areas and immature plantations. Our findings provide a valuable resource for stakeholders in the rubber industry, enabling efficient land management practices and sustainable agricultural development.

articleTitle: Advanced Design Pattern Selection Methodology through Weighted Semantic Ontologies for Microservices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Seamless communication between authorities, people, and smart devices is crucial in today's globally interconnected world. Unprecedented demands on software design result from the advent of ubiquitous connectivity, which allows connections at any time and from any location. By structuring applications as separate services that can communicate both internally inside a platform and externally across platforms, microservices (MS) architecture satisfies these requirements. One of the most difficult parts, though, is still controlling communication between MS services, which calls for knowledge of the best design patterns. In order to solve this, we suggest a context-aware recommender system that is adapted to MS design patterns. This system not only makes recommendations for appropriate patterns, but it also gives statistical scores that show how relevant each solution is to the particular issue at hand. Other patterns with ratings indicating their possible feasibility are also displayed by our algorithm. On the other hand, sentence transformers handle intricate, human-like problem descriptions, while our method uses MS Domain Ontologies to distinguish pattern applications, constraints, and best practices. Our methodology provides a refined examination of solution suitability and recommendations through the use of weighing and correlation algorithms. Extensively tested with more than 237 developer-style scenarios, our framework offers qualitative and quantitative insights into its performance and efficacy, showing notable gains over current solutions in terms of offering pattern-specific, contextually accurate guidance for MS communication challenges.

articleTitle: Data Partitioning and Storage Strategies for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications: A Review of Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: This paper presents a review of data partitioning and storage strategies critical for optimizing the performance and scalability of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) applications. As the volume and complexity of data continue to grow, effective data management becomes increasingly essential for ensuring the efficiency and accuracy of AI/ML models. The review categorizes and evaluates various data partitioning techniques, including hash-based, range-based and graph-based algorithms, highlighting their strengths, weaknesses, and suitability for different types of datasets and applications. It also explores the data processing challenges with AI/ML applications, data access patterns for AI/ML algorithms; and implementation techniques and evaluation metrics. By identifying key factors that influence the choice of partitioning and storage strategies, this review provides valuable insights for researchers and practitioners seeking to enhance the performance of AI/ML systems. The review also serves as a foundation for future research and development, guiding the design of more efficient and scalable data management solutions in artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Improving IT Service Governance in the ETLE System by Applying the Integration ITIL and COBIT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: The implementation of Electronic Traffic Law Enforcement (ETLE) plays an important role in supporting smart city programs to improve road safety in the region. However, the implementation of IT-based services in the ETLE system still requires thorough evaluation and analysis, particularly due to challenges in the tools component. The analysis was conducted using a methodology developed based on the ITIL V4 and COBIT 2019 frameworks. The service capability levels for change enablement, incident management, service desk, and problem management are currently at level 1 and have not yet reached the fully achieved category. Therefore, a gap analysis was performed along with the formulation of recommendations to improve IT service management processes, aiming to optimize IT services. The proposed improvement of procedures, by implementing the principles of good governance and grounded in the ITIL V4 and COBIT 2019 frameworks, indicates that well-documented service management processes can guide the enhancement of the ETLE system while reducing dependence on vendors.

articleTitle: Intelligent Decision Support System for Crime Investigation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer and Applications (ICCA)
abstract: Crime presents one of society's most formidable challenges, with its escalating rates significantly impacting individuals, families, and communities in detrimental ways.
